source.title: DropAttack: A Masked Weight Adversarial Training Method to Improve Generalization of Neural Networks
source.authors: Shi-Wen Ni; Jia-Wen Li; Hung-Yu Kao

record.tranche_reason: The study directly applies dropout to image and text classifiers and compares their reported held-out performance with the corresponding unregularized models.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's dropout comparisons. DropAttack results, including its generalization improvements, do not test a listed version. The authors' discussion of dropout in the introduction and cited results are not treated as study results.
record.test_reason: Table 2 directly compares dropout with baseline training in convolutional image classifiers, testing V6 using held-out classification error. The recurrent text classifiers fall outside V6's stated architecture scope.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that DropAttack improves generalization and reduces overfitting, especially for NLP, and interpret their theoretical analysis as showing gradient regularization. These conclusions concern DropAttack rather than dropout.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares dropout regularization with unregularized models, but does not state the dropout configuration used for this comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Dropout increases reported accuracy in three recurrent text classifiers: IMDB 88.12% to 88.64%, PHEME 84.08% to 85.85%, and AGnews 91.87% to 92.22%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout can improve held-out performance in recurrent text classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: DropAttack improves held-out performance in the main comparisons, and the authors describe its test-loss landscapes as lower and flatter. These visualizations do not measure V7's training-error perturbation tolerance or rank generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Masked adversarial training can improve held-out performance and produce visually flatter test-loss landscapes.

record.problems: The dropout configuration and uncertainty statistics beyond the number of runs are not stated. The paper reports aggregate scores from five runs rather than per-run values.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible dropout comparison rows were left out.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Fully connected classifiers; very small training sets; excessive dropout; dropout configuration dependence; removing dropout and weight decay together with data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance measured through training error, its association with generalization gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V6. Table 2 reports results calculated from five runs but supplies no standard deviations, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The small-data experiments and attack-probability sweep concern DropAttack, so they do not test V6's small-data or excessive-dropout qualifications.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparisons.
Large versus small batch generalization comparisons.
The study does not test very small training sets, excessive dropout, or removing dropout and weight decay together with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
